title: Attachment Theory (Bowlby)
summary: Bowlby's attachment theory: attachment as an innate bond, attachment phases, attachment styles (secure, anxious-ambivalent, avoidant, disorganized) and internal working models.
objectives: Explain internal working models and attachment phases.
revision: Bowlby's attachment theory: attachment bond, four styles, internal working models, attachment phases.

notes.t: An enduring emotional bond between infant and caregiver that serves a survival function.

i: Secure: confident exploration, seeks comfort from caregiver
Anxious-ambivalent: clingy, distressed, hard to soothe
Avoidant: ignores caregiver, shows little emotion

notes.t: A mental representation of self and others formed from early attachment experiences.

i: Attachment-in-the-making (6 weeks-6 months): preference for familiar caregiver
Formation of reciprocal relationship (18 months-2 years): goal-corrected partnership

notes.t: UGC NET frequently asks about Bowlby's attachment theory and attachment styles.

mnemonics.title: SAAD
mnemonics.text: S — Secure, A — Anxious-ambivalent, A — Avoidant, D — Disorganized

flashcards.a: Enduring emotional bond infant-caregiver, survival function.
Mental representation of self and others from attachment.
